title: Local proxy & replayable sandbox strategies for SDK integration testing
author: Hannah Lee
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines recommended patterns for building local proxies, network shims, and replayable sandboxes used by SDK teams and integrators to test Redwood API integrations. The goal is to provide deterministic, low-friction environments for: fast developer iteration, CI integration tests, and deterministic regression tests for canonical fixes.

Audience
--------
- SDK engineers and maintainers
- QA engineers running integration and regression suites
- Developer platform engineers creating local tooling

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
- Goals:
  - Enable offline, deterministic playback of Redwood API responses.
  - Provide low-latency local proxies that can simulate rate limits, latency, and token cost metadata.
  - Offer a minimal, reusable config surface that SDKs can consume for consistent behavior across developer machines and CI.
- Non-goals:
  - Not intended to replace end-to-end smoke tests against the hosted Redwood API.
  - Not a substitute for Dedicated/Private environment testing for performance/SLA validation.

Patterns (high level)
---------------------
1) Local forward proxy (development):
   - Runs on developer laptop; forwards requests to real Redwood endpoints by default.
   - Supports response caching, header augmentation (X-Redwood-Mock: true), and latency injection.
   - Use case: fast local iteration with ability to toggle mock mode.

2) Replayable sandbox (deterministic):
   - Captures request/response pairs and stores them as replay fixtures.
   - On replay mode, responses are returned from fixtures with strict match rules (method, path, body hash).
   - Use case: CI regression tests and canonical-fix verification.

3) Network shim for chaos and policy testing:
   - Injects simulated network failures, 5xx responses, and rate-limit headers for resilience testing.
   - Runs in CI or as a sidecar in local compose stacks.

Implementation blueprint
------------------------
- Service name: devx-local-proxy (recommended)
- Language: Go or Node (we maintain a reference Node prototype at tools/devx/proxy)
- Config precedence: environment variables -> config file (~/.redwood/devx-proxy.yaml) -> CLI flags

Minimal config example (YAML)
---------------------------
mode: replay  # forward | replay | proxy
port: 4321
redwood_base_url: https://api.redwood.ai
fixture_dir: ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures
latency_ms: 0  # base latency to add for forward mode
strict_match: true

CLI examples
------------
# Start local proxy forwarding to production (developer laptop)
$ devx-proxy start --mode proxy --port 4321

# Record a session to fixtures (used in CI when creating canonical test cases)
$ devx-proxy record --fixture-name=canonical-2026-02-01 --out ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures/canonical-2026-02-01.json 

# Replay recorded session in CI
$ devx-proxy start --mode replay --fixture ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures/canonical-2026-02-01.json --port 4321

SDK integration quickstart (Node)
--------------------------------
1) Install local proxy (dev dependency):
   npm install --save-dev @redwood/devx-proxy

2) Start proxy during local development (package.json scripts):
   "scripts": {
     "dev:proxy": "devx-proxy start --mode proxy --port 4321"
   }

3) Point SDK to proxy in development: set REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:4321

Config matrix and requirements
------------------------------
| Setting            | Purpose                                     | Example value             | Notes |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| mode               | Choose behavior                              | proxy / replay / forward  | replay requires fixtures|
| fixture_dir        | Where recorded sessions live                 | ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures  | CI mountable path recommended|
| strict_match       | Whether to require exact body match          | true/false               | false tolerates timestamp differences|
| latency_ms         | Inject deterministic latency (ms)            | 0 / 50 / 200             | Useful for overhead tests|
| rate_limit_rps     | Simulate rate limiting (requests/sec)        | 10                       | Applies in shim mode|

Fixture format (summary)
------------------------
- Stored as JSONL (one entry per request) to make diffs small and streaming easy.
- Each entry: timestamp, request_method, request_path, request_body_hash, response_status, response_headers, response_body_base64.
- File names MUST be prefixed with team or SDK name (e.g., sdk-js-canonical-2026-02-01.jsonl).

Example fixture ingestion command (CI)
-----------------------------------
# Validate fixtures and upload to artifact storage (optional)
$ devx-proxy validate fixtures --dir ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures && devx-proxy upload fixtures --dir ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures --target s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/devx-fixtures/

Best practices and conventions
------------------------------
- All fixtures used in regression suites must include a metadata header comment with: created_by, created_at (ISO8601), sdk_version, canonical_issue_id (if applicable).
- Keep fixtures under 5MB for CI speed; split long sessions into multiple fixtures.
- Mark fixtures used in official canonical fixes with a naming convention: canonical-<issue>-<YYYYMMDD>.jsonl
- Don’t record secrets: the proxy automatically strips Authorization and API-Key headers from fixtures. If secrets are present, record will fail with non-zero exit code.

CI integration example (GitHub Actions)
-------------------------------------
- job: integration_tests
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Start replay proxy
      run: devx-proxy start --mode replay --fixture ~/.redwood/devx-fixtures/canonical-auth-flows.jsonl --port 4321 &
    - name: Run tests
      env:
        REDWOOD_API_BASE: http://localhost:4321
      run: npm run test:integration

Troubleshooting and canonical fixes workflow
------------------------------------------
1) Reproduce locally using devx-proxy record. If reproduction requires production-only behavior, capture a short session (<= 30s) and sanitize.
2) Create a fixture and run the SDK integration tests against it.
3) If tests pass locally but fail in CI, confirm environment parity: node version, env vars, and strict_match setting.
4) If behavior differs from hosted API, capture canonical failing request and open a canonical-fix PR with: fixture, failing test, triage notes, and suggested runtime change. Tag the PR with label: "canonical-fix".

Common issues and remedies
--------------------------
- Non-deterministic failures: set strict_match=false temporarily and normalize timestamps in fixtures.
- Authorization header stripped in fixture: the proxy will remove it; use token-mocking helpers in tests instead of recording real tokens.
- Large fixture slowdowns: split into smaller fixtures and parallelize CI jobs.

SLOs and metrics to observe
---------------------------
- Local proxy availability: target 99.9% during CI windows.
- Fixture validation success rate: target 100% pre-merge for canonical fixtures.
- CI integration test runtime delta when using replay vs real: target < 3x runtime overhead.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Owning team: devx-tooling (eng platform org).
- Primary owner: Hannah Lee (devx-tooling)
- Backup owner: Miguel Alvarez
- Escalation path: pager duty to eng-platform on-call -> devx-tooling SLA owner.

Rollout checklist for SDK teams
-------------------------------
1) Add devx-proxy as devDependency and a local start script.
2) Create at least one canonical fixture for critical flows and commit to fixtures repo or artifact storage.
3) Add replay stage to CI (must be green before merging changes touching SDK network layer).
4) Document the fixture used in the PR with metadata and link to canonical issue.

---------------------------

Appendix: small code snippets
----------------------------
# Simple Node proxy header injection (express):
```
const express = require('express')
const proxy = require('http-proxy-middleware')
const app = express()
app.use('/v1', (req, res, next) => {
  req.headers['x-devx'] = 'local-proxy'
  next()
}, proxy.createProxyMiddleware({ target: 'https://api.redwood.ai', changeOrigin: true }))
app.listen(4321)
```
